=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py: select() function, lines 340-373 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The documented 72-hour session age cutoff is not enforced in the selector; older sessions on the boundary page remain eligible for resume.
  WHY: A session created more than 3 days ago with a matching usage-limit status_detail can be selected and resumed ahead of recent sessions, consuming the per-wake quota.
- .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py: _bound_wakes, line 285 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: _bound_wakes reads only trigger.get("next_run_at"), which may be absent for one-shot triggers created with run_once_at.
  WHY: If next_run_at is absent, _parse_time(None) returns None and _wake_pending treats an unreadable time as imminent, causing a session bound to a far-future trigger to be skipped.
- .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py: CHECKER_PROMPT constant, lines 121-124 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The duplicate-stage guard checks one unpaginated page of 20 sessions and does not mention has_more or pagination.
  WHY: The resumed checker may not see its already-created child and may repeat the session-creation step.
- changelog.d/5660-resume-usage-limit-stops.md: line 28 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The claim “stalled projects resume within one pickup wake of the reset” overstates recovery speed when more sessions qualify than the per-wake cap.
  WHY: A reader may expect complete recovery in one wake while pending sessions remain for later pickup wakes.
- README.md: lines 1262-1285 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The usage-limit resume block separates the queue catch-up sentence from its concluding sentence, making “An issue” ambiguous.
  WHY: A reader could mistake the queue wait time as describing usage-limit resume latency.
- .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py: _decode_json_text, line 170 | HARDENING
  ISSUE: The no-JSON error does not name the MAX_JSON_START_CANDIDATES cap, making it indistinguishable from genuinely malformed input in the pickup's limit_pending=unknown report.
  SUGGESTED MINIMAL FIX: Include the cap value: f"{path}: no JSON object or array found in the first {MAX_JSON_START_CANDIDATES} candidate positions"
- .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py: _parse_time, line 183 | HARDENING
  ISSUE: The magic number 1e12 for distinguishing seconds from milliseconds is undocumented.
  SUGGESTED MINIMAL FIX: Extract to a module constant EPOCH_MS_THRESHOLD = 1e12 with a one-line comment.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py: lines 349-373 (in select()) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The selector does not check created_at or enforce the documented 72-hour session cutoff against the current time.
  WHY: Stale sessions from the boundary page remain eligible and can consume the 20-session per-wake quota ahead of fresh sessions.
- changelog.d/5660-resume-usage-limit-stops.md: line 28 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The statement that stalled projects resume “within one pickup wake of the reset” is inaccurate when qualifying sessions exceed the per-wake cap.
  WHY: With a default cap of 20 and an incident stopping 47 sessions, at least three wakes are required to clear the backlog.
- README.md: lines 1267-1285 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The usage-limit resume block separates the queue catch-up explanation from its concluding sentence.
  WHY: “An issue therefore waits up to about an hour before its session starts...” may appear to describe resumed sessions rather than the queue's hourly wake.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py: lines 121-124 (CHECKER_PROMPT constant) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The duplicate-stage guard inspects only one unpaginated page of 20 sessions.
  WHY: If the existing child session is beyond page 1, the checker may create a duplicate stage or fixer session.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py: line 285 (in _bound_wakes) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: _bound_wakes checks only trigger.get("next_run_at") and does not fall back to trigger.get("run_once_at").
  WHY: A missing next_run_at is parsed as None and treated as an unreadable/imminent wake, falsely skipping a session bound to a future one-shot trigger.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py: line 170 (_decode_json_text) | HARDENING
  ISSUE: InputError on no JSON object found does not mention MAX_JSON_START_CANDIDATES, making cap exhaustion indistinguishable from malformed input.
  SUGGESTED MINIMAL FIX: Include MAX_JSON_START_CANDIDATES in the error message.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py: lines 193-194 (_parse_time) | HARDENING
  ISSUE: The magic number 1e12 used to distinguish seconds from milliseconds is unexplained at the call site.
  SUGGESTED MINIMAL FIX: Extract EPOCH_MS_THRESHOLD = 1e12 as a named constant with a brief comment.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py: select() function, the `for position, session in enumerate(sessions):` per-session loop (the script body around the for loop; the script never inspects `created_at`). | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The selector does not filter sessions older than the promised 72-hour / 3-day cutoff by created_at.
  WHY: An already-stale session on a fetched boundary page can be resumed while a fresh stop waits for the next hour.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py: CHECKER_PROMPT constant, lines 121-124 (the duplicate-stage guard instruction "call list_sessions (mine: true, limit: 20)"). | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The duplicate-stage guard reads only one page of 20 sessions and does not instruct the resumed checker to inspect has_more or paginate; it also lacks a source_url / repository check.
  WHY: If the child is beyond page 1, the checker may repeat session creation; a same-titled session from another repository could also be mistaken for the intended child.
- changelog.d/5660-resume-usage-limit-stops.md: line 28, "What this means for operators" paragraph ("after a usage-limit stop, stalled projects resume within one pickup wake of the reset"). | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The closing paragraph asserts recovery completes in a single wake despite the documented 20-session cap and 47-session incident.
  WHY: Only the first 20 sessions can resume on the first wake; the remaining sessions wait for later wakes.
- README.md: lines 1262-1285, the inserted usage-limit resume block between "a catch-up wake never schedules another (#4990)." and "An issue therefore waits up to about an hour before its session starts...". | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The inserted block breaks the antecedent of the next sentence, leaving “An issue” ambiguous and splitting the queue explanation.
  WHY: Operators can misread the queue wait-time statement as describing usage-limit resume latency.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py: line 170, `raise InputError(f"{path}: no JSON object or array found")` inside `_decode_json_text`. | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The error does not identify that the MAX_JSON_START_CANDIDATES = 50 cap was exhausted.
  WHY: A future envelope with more than 50 non-JSON prefix characters could make valid list_sessions data appear malformed without indicating the cause.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py: line 161, `positions = [index for index, char in enumerate(text) if char in "{["][:MAX_JSON_START_CANDIDATES]`. | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The list comprehension scans the full input to collect every `{` or `[` position before the slice limits the list.
  WHY: The cap does not save the comprehension pass, although the slice still bounds the JSON-decode loop and there is no correctness impact.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py: `_bound_wakes`, the line `wakes.setdefault(session_id, []).append(_parse_time(trigger.get("next_run_at")))`. | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The selector reads
